findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without a lock while the watch goroutine can write to it
findings.body:
`bleveBackend.TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`. This PR adds a call to it in `searchSupport.init` (search.go:216), after the watch goroutine has already started at search.go:207.

That goroutine calls `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex`, which now writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()` (bleve.go:137-139). If a write event arrives for a resource that has no index yet, the map write can overlap with the unlocked iteration in `TotalDocs`.

Go treats concurrent map iteration and write as a fatal, unrecoverable runtime error, so this can crash the process at startup. `TotalDocs` should take `b.cacheMu.RLock()`, or the log line should run before the watcher is started.

findings.title: Errgroup workers share and overwrite the outer `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` variables
findings.body:
Inside `group.Go`, each worker assigns to the enclosing function's `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and returns it, and also increments `totalBatchesIndexed++` without synchronization.

Before this PR, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `cacheMu` for its entire duration, which effectively serialized most of the work. This PR removes that lock so builds really run in parallel with up to `initWorkers` goroutines, which widens the race window considerably.

One worker can overwrite `err` between another worker's assignment and its `return err`. A failed index build can then be reported as success, letting startup continue with a missing index, or a successful worker can return another worker's error. The `namespaced_indexed` span attribute is also racy.

Fix: use a local variable (`_, _, err := s.build(...)`) and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Stop() no longer causes requests to be rejected because handlers stopped checking Init
findings.body:
`Stop` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". This was the mechanism that made subsequent gRPC calls fail, because every handler called `s.Init(ctx)` and the already-completed `sync.Once` returned `initErr`.

This PR removes the `Init` call from all handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob), and nothing else reads `initErr`. After `Stop`, requests are still served against a backend whose lifecycle has been stopped and whose watch context is cancelled. `IsHealthy` also keeps reporting healthy during shutdown.

If stop semantics are still wanted, keep a cheap check of a stopped/initErr flag in the handlers (protected against the data race with `Stop`).

findings.title: Init failure in the constructor leaks the cancel func and background watchers
findings.body:
`NewResourceServer` now runs `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure without calling `s.cancel()` or `lifecycle.Stop`.

If `search.init` succeeds and `initWatcher` then fails, the search watcher has already been started: it called `WatchWriteEvents` with `context.Background()`, and its backend poller goroutine runs until the backend is stopped. Because the server is never returned, nobody can stop it. The cancelable context created for the server is also never cancelled.

Call `cancel()` and stop the lifecycle hooks on the error path.

findings.title: Postgres integration test disabled instead of fixed
findings.body:
This PR adds an unconditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer`, noting that it "works locally".

The PR moves resource server initialization (DB init and migrations, building indexes for every namespace, starting watchers) into the constructor, which runs during `InitializeModuleServer`. A CI failure that appears together with this change is likely related to it, for example a timeout or a connection issue at construction time.

Skipping the test removes postgres coverage of the storage-server target exactly when its startup behaviour changes. The root cause should be investigated, or at least tracked with an issue link, rather than silently skipped.
